rankedFamilies.basis: All fourteen authored experiences ask the learner to interpret or assemble ordered qualitative graph segments. A single finite segment truth can preserve every graph direction, rate, flat interval, curvature, order, misconception, remedial route, and seeded form without changing the assessed action.

The numerical closure is larger, but the lessons do not share one learner action: one tests proportionality/invariants while the other coordinates contextual tables and covariation. A single mutation would either collapse modelling into table recognition or require multiple engines.

Both compare functions, but authored claims cross tables, equations, graphs, rates, and initial values. One graph-segment model cannot preserve those representations; the exact solution is a multi-representation functionCompareLab, not this session's pure segment closure.
Back-substitution is a symbolic construction pipeline, while real-world systems require modelling and intersection interpretation. They can share systems truth but not one exact interaction grammar.

Remainder interpretation and decimal long division share arithmetic ancestry but not authored claims or misconception routes. A combined engine needs independently complete context and algorithm modes.

Both fit a rounding band, but one explicitly compares estimates and the other applies rounding in context. Existing number-line extensions remain preferable and do not yield the same renderer-to-narration breakthrough.
rankedFamilies.rejectionRisk: extension, not shared new truth closure

selectedLessonProofs.title: Reading Graph Shapes
selectedLessonProofs.acceptanceContract: Classified from the authored prompts. Acceptance contract: The graph shape must be rendered; steepness, direction, and flatness must be traceable.

authoredWrongPaths.feedback: That would be a graph curving upward more steeply, not a flat line.
Steady speed is a straight SLANTED line — flat means not moving at all.
Moving backward would slope DOWN — a flat line means no movement.
Steeper means FASTER, not slower — a gentle slope would be slow.
Standing still is a FLAT section — steep means fast movement.
Turning around would slope downward — steep upward means fast forward movement.
Increasing would slope UP — a downward slope means it's falling.
Constant is a FLAT line — a downward slope means decreasing.
Rising then falling would go up then down — a steady downward slope is just decreasing.
It's still RISING (increasing) — just more slowly; decreasing would slope down.
Getting less steep means SLOWING down, not speeding up.
It's still rising, just gently — a completely flat graph wouldn't rise at all.
Steep upward means riding away fast — not stopped.
Gentle upward means riding away slowly — still moving, not stopped.
Downward means heading back toward home — moving, not stopped.

selectedLessonProofs.title: Sketching Graphs from Stories
selectedLessonProofs.acceptanceContract: Classified from the authored prompts. Acceptance contract: Learner must assemble stages in order and see the resulting graph, not choose verbal labels.

authoredWrongPaths.feedback: That's the reverse order — it FILLS first (rising), THEN holds (flat).
The water never decreases here — it rises, then holds steady.
Steady filling is a straight line, not a steepening curve — then it goes flat.
The car is moving the whole time — distance rises throughout, first curving, then straight.
The car never stops — after speeding up it keeps moving, so the line keeps rising (doesn't go flat).
Distance from the start INCREASES as the car drives — the graph rises, not falls.
It LOSES height first (falling), lands (flat), then rises — three stages, starting downward.
The height changes in stages — it can't be flat throughout.
It starts by LOSING height (falling), so it can't rise the whole time.
Steady pace is a STRAIGHT line (constant rate), not a steepening curve; then flat for the stop.
They walk FIRST (rising), then stop (flat) — this has the order reversed.
Distance increases while walking (rising), not falling; then flat when stopped.
A straight line means the SAME growth each year — here it grows by MORE each year, so it curves.
Flat means no growth — but the savings grow (and speed up), so it rises and steepens.
Falling means shrinking — the savings GROW, so the graph rises (and steepens).
That reverses fast and slow — it drives FAST first (steep), then SLOW last (gentle).
Stopping at a light is FLAT, not falling — the car doesn't go backward.
The car drives FIRST (steep rise), then stops (flat) — it doesn't start out stopped.
